An analysis of ClickUp alternatives characterizes Plane as free and self-hostable with a modern interface covering issues, cycles, modules, and roadmaps, but cautions that its documentation and goals features are lighter than ClickUp’s and its ecosystem is newer.

The Plane blog claims full feature parity with Jira Standard and eighty percent parity with Jira Professional, along with more than fifty thousand self-hosting teams, over one hundred thousand Docker deploys, and forty-four thousand Kubernetes deploys.
The Plane blog also says Plane includes artificial intelligence, documentation, intake, and time tracking as native built-in features rather than afterthought plugins.

A review of open-source project management tools calls Plane the nearest open-source equivalent to Linear and Jira Software, citing fifty-nine thousand one hundred sixteen GitHub stars and near-weekly releases.
Heise Online notes that Plane markets itself as an open-source alternative to Jira, Linear, Monday, and Asana.

An INNOQ review states Plane offers a clean, organized user experience that the reviewer would choose first for self-hosted agile project management, though the reviewer considers it a relatively young project compared with more mature Jira replacements.
